docs.title: API Standard Starter
docs.text:
Enterprise-grade API standardization and error intelligence for Spring Boot.

api-standard-spring-boot-starter is a library designed to standardize API error handling in Spring Boot applications by enforcing strict compliance with RFC 9457 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs).

It provides a unified contract for error responses, automatic PII redaction, and a passive system load indicator.

docs.title: The Problem It Resolves
docs.text:
In distributed systems and microservices, inconsistent error responses lead to: * Contract Drift: Different endpoints or services returning different JSON structures for similar errors. * Traceability Gaps: Errors lacking a unified correlation ID, making log aggregation and debugging difficult. * Information Leakage: Accidental exposure of internal stack traces or database details in production responses.

This starter provides a centralized mechanism to handle exceptions and render them in a predictable, machine-readable format.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
The library provides the following features based on the current codebase:

  • RFC 9457 Compliance: All handled errors return a ProblemDetail body with standard fields (type, title, status, detail, instance).
  • Error Codes: Maps exceptions to a set of canonical error codes (e.g., INTERNAL_ERROR, VALIDATION_ERROR, NOT_FOUND).
  • Trace ID Injection: Automatically injects a traceId from the MDC into the error response.
  • PII Redaction: Masks sensitive fields (like password, creditCard, token) in validation error details.
  • Degraded Mode Indicator: Adds a header or JSON flag when system CPU usage exceeds a configurable threshold.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The library operates as a non-intrusive layer on top of Spring MVC:

  1. Interception: A @ControllerAdvice (GlobalExceptionHandler) intercepts thrown exceptions.
  2. Enrichment: A pipeline of ProblemDetailEnricher beans (such as StandardMetadataEnricher and TraceIdEnricher) adds operational metadata to the response.
  3. Serialization: The final ProblemDetail is serialized as JSON.

docs.title: Benchmarks & Production Cases
docs.text: [!NOTE] Specific benchmark metrics (latency overhead, throughput capacity) and specific company case studies are not available in the current project source code or documentation. The library is designed to be lightweight by minimizing object allocations in the exception handling path, but no official performance numbers are declared.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
When a validation fails, the library produces a response like this:

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:validation-error",
  "title": "Validation Error",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Invalid request content.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/resource",
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "traceId": "d8b3a0e1c2d3e4f5",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-18T21:27:00Z"
}

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This section provides a rigorous, production-grade API reference for the core components of the api-standard-spring-boot-starter.

docs.title: 1. BusinessException
docs.text: Signals a business-rule violation that should be communicated to the caller with a specific HTTP status code and ErrorCode.

docs.title: Complete Signature
docs.text:
public class BusinessException extends ProblemException {
  public BusinessException(ErrorCode code, String message, HttpStatus status);
  public BusinessException(String message, HttpStatus status);
  public BusinessException(String message, HttpStatus status, String customUrl);
  public BusinessException(ErrorCode code, String message, HttpStatus status, String type);
  public BusinessException(ErrorCode code, String message, HttpStatus status, URI type);

  public static Builder builder(String message);
}

docs.title: Parameters (Main Constructor)
docs.text: Name Type Required Default Description code ErrorCode Yes Derived from status The machine-readable canonical error code. message String Yes - User-friendly detail message or i18n translation key. status HttpStatus Yes BAD_REQUEST The HTTP status to return to the client.

docs.title: Returns & Contracts
docs.text:
• Shape: Extends RuntimeException.
  • Mutability: Immutable once instantiated.
  • Lifecycle: Ephemeral. Created at the moment of failure, caught by GlobalExceptionHandler, and immediately garbage collected after the response is rendered.
  • Ownership: Owned by the domain/application layer throwing it.

docs.title: Throws
docs.text: As an exception itself, it is meant to be thrown. * Retryability: Generally not retryable without modifying the request (since it represents a business rule violation, e.g., 409 Conflict or 422 Validation Error). * Recoverability: Handled automatically by the starter's global handler.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Complejidad (Complexity): $O(1)$.
  • Allocations: Minimal, but involves standard JVM stack trace generation which is relatively heavy.
  • Impacto Runtime: Designed for exceptional flows. Should not be used for normal control flow to avoid stack trace generation overhead.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Validación: Requires non-null message if using the Builder.
  • Unsafe Patterns: Do not pass raw user input or PII directly into the message field unless it's a translation key, as this message is exposed directly to the HTTP client.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Nullability: If code is passed as null in the constructor, it resolves to a default based on the HTTP status.
  • Translation Fallback: If the message is intended to be an i18n key but the key is not found in messages.properties, the key itself is returned to the user.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Basic Example 

if (user.isBanned()) {
    throw new BusinessException(ErrorCode.FORBIDDEN, "User is currently banned", HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}

Advanced Example (Builder) 

throw BusinessException.builder("error.payment.insufficient_funds")
    .status(HttpStatus.PAYMENT_REQUIRED)
    .code(ErrorCode.VALIDATION_ERROR)
    .type(URI.create("https://docs.mycompany.com/errors/funds"))
    .build();

docs.title: 2. ProblemDetailEnricher
docs.text: The primary extension hook for adding custom metadata to all RFC 9457 error responses.

docs.title: Complete Signature
docs.text:
public interface ProblemDetailEnricher {
  default void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale);
  default void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale, Exception ex);
  default int order();
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Default Description problem ProblemDetail Yes - The mutable problem detail object to enrich. request HttpServletRequest Yes - The current HTTP request context. locale Locale Yes - The resolved locale for the request. ex Exception No null The original exception that triggered the error.

docs.title: Returns & Contracts
docs.text:
• Mutabilidad: Implementations must mutate the injected ProblemDetail object (typically using problem.setProperty()).
  • Lifecycle: Beans implementing this interface are collected at application startup. The enrich method is called synchronously on every error request.
  • Order: Governed by the order() method (lower values execute first).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Bottlenecks: Because this runs synchronously in the Servlet thread during error handling, implementations must not perform blocking I/O (e.g., database calls or HTTP requests).
  • Caching: If enrichment requires reference data, it must be cached aggressively in memory.

docs.title: Seguridad
docs.text: • Sanitización: Any data extracted from HttpServletRequest (e.g., headers) and injected into the response must be sanitized to prevent Log Forging or XSS (though Spring's JSON serializer handles basic escaping).

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Stale State: If extracting data from SecurityContextHolder, be aware that the context might be partially cleared or empty if the error occurred very early in the filter chain.
  • Nullability: ex can be null in some synthetic error scenarios.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Built-in Trace ID Enrichment (from library source) 

@Component
public class TraceIdEnricher implements ProblemDetailEnricher {
    @Override
    public void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale) {
        String traceId = MDC.get("traceId");
        if (traceId != null) {
            problem.setProperty("traceId", traceId);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public int order() {
        return 100;
    }
}

docs.title: 3. ErrorCode
docs.text: Canonical enumeration of supported error identifiers.

docs.title: Complete Signature
docs.text:
public enum ErrorCode {
  INTERNAL_ERROR, BAD_REQUEST, VALIDATION_ERROR, GONE, UNAUTHORIZED, 
  FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, 
  CONFLICT, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, BAD_GATEWAY, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, GATEWAY_TIMEOUT;

  public static ErrorCode fromStatus(int status);
  public String toKebabCase();
}

docs.title: Returns & Contracts
docs.text:
• Shape: Java enum.
  • Mutabilidad: Strictly immutable.
  • Contratos: Designed to provide a finite, machine-readable vocabulary for error classification across the organization.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text: • Status Fallback (fromStatus): If an unrecognized HTTP status is passed (e.g., 418), it falls back to BAD_REQUEST if the status is 4xx, and INTERNAL_ERROR otherwise.

docs.title: 4. ApiStandardProperties
docs.text: The @ConfigurationProperties class that governs the library's behavior.

docs.title: Complete Signature
docs.text:
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "api.standard")
public class ApiStandardProperties {
    public Errors getErrors();
    public DegradedMode getDegradedMode();
    public Redaction getRedaction();
}

(For a full list of YAML/Properties parameters, refer to the Installation guide).

docs.title: Lifecycle & Mutability
docs.text:
• Lifecycle: Instantiated once during Spring Boot context initialization.
  • Mutabilidad: Fields are mutable via setters (required by Spring Boot), but modifying them programmatically post-startup is an anti-pattern and may lead to inconsistent behavior across threads.

docs.title: Fundamental Concepts
docs.text:
Understanding the internal architecture of api-standard-spring-boot-starter is key to extending it and using it effectively in production.

This library is built upon the Open/Closed Principle (OCP) and acts as a non-intrusive layer over Spring MVC.

docs.title: Internal Architecture & Pipeline
docs.text: The error handling process follows a strict, predictable pipeline designed to standardize every exception thrown during an HTTP request.

docs.title: The Lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Controller
    participant GlobalExceptionHandler
    participant ProblemDetailService
    participant Enrichers

    Client->>Controller: HTTP Request
    Controller-->>GlobalExceptionHandler: Throws Exception
    GlobalExceptionHandler->>ProblemDetailService: createProblem(status, exception)

    rect rgb(30, 40, 50)
    Note over ProblemDetailService,Enrichers: Enrichment Pipeline
    ProblemDetailService->>ProblemDetailService: 1. Resolve i18n Title & Detail
    ProblemDetailService->>ProblemDetailService: 2. Resolve Type URI
    ProblemDetailService->>Enrichers: enrich(problem, request, locale, ex)
    Enrichers-->>ProblemDetailService: Add Custom Metadata (traceId, degraded)
    end

    ProblemDetailService-->>GlobalExceptionHandler: Enriched ProblemDetail
    GlobalExceptionHandler-->>Client: JSON Response (RFC 9457)

docs.title: 1. Interception Phase
docs.text:
The GlobalExceptionHandler is a @RestControllerAdvice registered with the Ordered.LOWEST_PRECEDENCE. This means it will catch any exception not explicitly handled by your own custom @ControllerAdvice classes.

It explicitly handles: * ProblemException (and BusinessException). * Validation errors (MethodArgumentNotValidException, ConstraintViolationException). * Spring MVC routing errors (404, 405, 415). * Resilience4j errors (CallNotPermittedException, RequestNotPermitted). * Any unhandled Exception (fallback to 500).

docs.title: 2. Processing Phase
docs.text: The ProblemDetailService acts as the core orchestrator. It creates a native Spring ProblemDetail object and applies core translations using Spring's MessageSource.

docs.title: 3. Enrichment Phase (Extensibility)
docs.text:
This is where the library shines. Instead of hardcoding fields like traceId or system load indicators into the core service, it delegates to a pipeline of ProblemDetailEnricher beans.

The library ships with several built-in enrichers: * StandardMetadataEnricher: Injects the code and timestamp. * TraceIdEnricher: Extracts the correlation ID from the logging MDC. * DegradedModeEnricher: Injects the degraded flag if the CPU load is high.

docs.title: Threading and Concurrency Model
docs.text:
This library operates entirely within the standard Servlet thread-per-request model (e.g., Tomcat, Undertow).

  • Stateless: All handler and service beans are stateless singletons.
  • No Custom Thread Pools: The library does not spawn its own threads or asynchronous boundaries. Error processing happens synchronously on the thread that threw the exception, ensuring MDC context (like Trace IDs) remains attached.
  • Performance: Object allocations are kept to a minimum in the critical path to avoid adding latency to error responses.

docs.title: Degraded Mode (Active Load Protection)
docs.text:
The library includes a passive system load indicator.

  1. A SystemLoadMonitor (implemented by DefaultSystemLoadMonitor) periodically checks the underlying JVM operating system metrics (OperatingSystemMXBean.getCpuLoad()).
  2. If the load exceeds the configured threshold (default 80%), a DegradedModeFilter adds the X-API-Degraded: true header to responses.
  3. Simultaneously, the DegradedModeEnricher adds "degraded": true to any error JSON emitted.

[!NOTE] If the host OS or JVM does not support getCpuLoad() (returning -1), the library assumes a normal load state.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• RFC 9457 Strictness: We never mutate the standard top-level fields (type, title, status, detail, instance) to mean something else. Custom data goes into extended properties.
  • Open/Closed Principle: You can add new fields to the JSON by creating a new ProblemDetailEnricher bean, without touching the core exception handler.

docs.title: Contributing Guide
docs.text: Thank you for considering contributing to the api-standard-spring-boot-starter. This library is a core infrastructure component, meaning stability and backward compatibility are our highest priorities.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21 (LTS) or higher.
  • Maven 3.8+

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The project is divided into three main modules: * api-standard-core: Contains the interfaces (ProblemDetailEnricher), ErrorCode, and the ProblemDetailService. (No Web/MVC dependencies). * api-standard-web: Contains the @RestControllerAdvice, GlobalExceptionHandler, and filters. (Depends on Spring Web). * api-standard-starter: The auto-configuration module. Contains spring.factories / AutoConfiguration.imports that wire everything together when the dependency is added.

docs.title: Build and Test
docs.text:
To compile the project and run all unit tests: 

mvn clean install

docs.title: 2. Testing and Coverage
docs.text:
Due to its role as a cross-cutting concern, we require extremely high reliability.

  • 100% Core Coverage: Any new Enricher or modification to ProblemDetailService must be accompanied by unit tests covering positive cases, negative cases, and null/edge bounds.
  • No Flaky Tests: Tests must not rely on Thread.sleep() or external network calls.

docs.title: 3. Release Flow and Standards
docs.text: This repository strictly adheres to automated semantic versioning.

docs.title: Conventional Commits
docs.text:
All pull requests and commits must follow the Conventional Commits specification. This allows our CI/CD pipeline to automatically generate changelogs and bump versions.

Valid Examples: * feat: add support for WebFlux exception handling (Will trigger a MINOR bump: 2.x.0) * fix: resolve NullPointerException in TraceIdEnricher (Will trigger a PATCH bump: 2.0.x) * feat!: completely redesign the ErrorCode enum (The ! indicates a BREAKING CHANGE, triggering a MAJOR bump: 3.0.0)

docs.title: Pull Request Process
docs.text:
1. Create a feature branch from main.
  2. Write your code and add necessary tests.
  3. Ensure mvn clean verify passes locally.
  4. Submit a Pull Request.
  5. Wait for the CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) to pass the build and SonarQube quality gates.
  6. Once approved by a maintainer, it will be Squash-Merged into main.

docs.title: Cookbook: Practical Recipes 👨‍🍳
docs.text: All recipes in this cookbook are taken directly from the sample-project included in this repository. Every code example has been verified against the real codebase.

docs.title: The Core Concept: ProblemDetailEnricher
docs.text:
Instead of modifying the core error handler, the library provides a simple interface called ProblemDetailEnricher.

Spring Boot automatically detects any class in your project that implements this interface. When an error occurs, the library passes the ProblemDetail object to your class, allowing you to add custom fields (properties) before the JSON is sent to the client.

docs.title: Recipe 1: Injecting a Static Application Name
docs.text: Scenario: You have multiple microservices using this library, and you want every error response to explicitly state which microservice generated the error.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
Create a new class in your configuration package:

package com.example.config;

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ProblemDetailEnricher;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import java.util.Locale;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class AppNameEnricher implements ProblemDetailEnricher {

    @Override
    public void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale) {
        // Add a static string identifying this microservice
        problem.setProperty("service", "billing-api");
    }

    @Override
    public int order() {
        // 100 ensures it runs after the built-in enrichers.
        return 100; 
    }
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
When an error happens, your JSON will now automatically include the "service" field:

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:bad-request",
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Invalid parameters.",
  "traceId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad",
  "service": "billing-api" 
}

docs.title: Recipe 2: Throwing Business Exceptions with ErrorCode
docs.text:
Scenario: Your domain logic detects a business rule violation (e.g., duplicate resource, insufficient permissions) and you need to communicate it cleanly to the API client.

Source: ExceptionDemoController.java

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Option A: Using the canonical ErrorCode enum
@GetMapping("/business-logic")
public void throwBusiness() {
    throw new BusinessException(
        ErrorCode.BAD_REQUEST, "Business rule violated.", HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
}

// Option B: Using ProblemException with automatic URN generation
@GetMapping("/problem-internal")
public void throwInternal() {
    // Automatically generates: urn:problem-type:too-many-requests
    throw new ProblemException("Rate limit reached.", HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
}

// Option C: Using a custom documentation URL instead of the auto-generated URN
@GetMapping("/problem-external")
public void throwExternal() {
    throw new ProblemException(
        "Validation error.",
        HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST,
        "https://docs.saul.dev/errors/validation-guide");
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:bad-request",
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Business rule violated.",
  "instance": "/api/demo/exceptions/business-logic",
  "code": "BAD_REQUEST",
  "traceId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-18T21:34:00Z"
}

docs.title: Recipe 3: i18n — Automatic Message Translation
docs.text:
Scenario: Your API supports multiple languages. You want error messages to automatically translate based on the client's Accept-Language header, without changing any controller code.

Source: ExceptionDemoController.java + messages.properties

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
Step 1: Define your keys in messages.properties and messages_es.properties:

# messages.properties (English - default)
sample.error.limit_reached=The project limit has been reached for user {0}.
error.user.already_exists=User with this email address is already registered.

# messages_es.properties (Spanish)
sample.error.limit_reached=Se ha alcanzado el límite del proyecto para el usuario {0}.
error.user.already_exists=El usuario con este correo ya se encuentra registrado.

Step 2: Throw the exception using the i18n key as the message:

// The library will resolve "sample.error.limit_reached" from messages.properties
@GetMapping("/client-key")
public void throwClientKey() {
    throw new BusinessException(
        ErrorCode.FORBIDDEN, "sample.error.limit_reached", HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
With Accept-Language: es:

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:forbidden",
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "Se ha alcanzado el límite del proyecto para el usuario {0}.",
  "code": "FORBIDDEN",
  "traceId": "..."
}

Note: If the key is not found in messages.properties, the raw string is returned as-is to the client, allowing fully custom messages without properties files.

docs.title: Recipe 4: Bean Validation with Automatic Error Details
docs.text:
Scenario: You want structured, detailed validation error responses when a client sends invalid JSON or query parameters.

Source: ValidationDemoController.java + UserDto.java

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
DTO with JSR-303 annotations: 

public class UserDto {
    @NotBlank(message = "Username cannot be blank")
    @Size(min = 3, max = 50, message = "Username must be between 3 and 50 characters")
    private String username;

    @NotNull(message = "Age is required")
    private Integer age;
}

Controller using @Valid: 

@PostMapping("/body")
public UserDto testBodyValidation(@Valid @RequestBody UserDto dto) {
    return dto;
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
Send POST /api/demo/validation/body with {"username": "", "age": null}:

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:validation-error",
  "title": "Validation Error",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "username: Username cannot be blank; age: Age is required",
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "traceId": "..."
}

Important: The Redaction Engine will automatically mask values for fields matching configured sensitive names (e.g., password, token, secret).

docs.title: Recipe 5: Feign Client Error Propagation
docs.text:
Scenario: Microservice A calls Microservice B via Feign. B fails. You need the error to propagate cleanly to the original caller without losing context.

Source: FeignDemoController.java

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The library automatically detects FeignException on the classpath and intercepts it:

  • Client errors (4xx): Propagated as-is (e.g., 404 → 404).
  • Server errors (5xx) or unknown: Transformed into 502 Bad Gateway to avoid exposing internal details.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// This simulates an upstream 503 failure → the library returns 502 Bad Gateway
@GetMapping("/upstream-failure")
public void throwFeignServiceUnavailable() {
    throw new feign.FeignException.ServiceUnavailable(
        "Upstream service down",
        feign.Request.create(
            feign.Request.HttpMethod.GET, "/external/api",
            java.util.Collections.emptyMap(), null, null, null),
        null, null);
}

// This simulates an upstream 404 → the library propagates it as 404
@GetMapping("/upstream-notfound")
public void throwFeignNotFound() {
    throw new feign.FeignException.NotFound(
        "Resource not found in remote service",
        feign.Request.create(
            feign.Request.HttpMethod.GET, "/remote-resource",
            java.util.Collections.emptyMap(), null, null, null),
        null, null);
}

docs.title: Recipe 6: Resilience4j Exception Handling
docs.text:
Scenario: Your API uses Resilience4j for circuit breakers, rate limiters, or bulkheads. When these mechanisms trip, you need clean RFC 9457 responses instead of raw stack traces.

Source: ResilienceDemoController.java

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The GlobalExceptionHandler natively detects and maps Resilience4j exceptions:

Exception HTTP Status Error Code CallNotPermittedException 503 Service Unavailable SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE RequestNotPermitted 429 Too Many Requests TOO_MANY_REQUESTS BulkheadFullException 429 Too Many Requests TOO_MANY_REQUESTS TimeoutException 504 Gateway Timeout GATEWAY_TIMEOUT

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
@GetMapping("/circuit-breaker")
public void circuitBreaker() {
    CircuitBreaker cb = CircuitBreaker.ofDefaults("demo-circuit");
    throw CallNotPermittedException.createCallNotPermittedException(cb);
}

@GetMapping("/rate-limiter")
public void rateLimiter() {
    RateLimiter limit = RateLimiter.of("demo-rate",
        RateLimiterConfig.custom()
            .limitForPeriod(1)
            .limitRefreshPeriod(Duration.ofSeconds(1))
            .build());
    throw RequestNotPermitted.createRequestNotPermitted(limit);
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:too-many-requests",
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "RequestNotPermitted: ...",
  "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS",
  "traceId": "..."
}

docs.title: Recipe 7: Custom Exception with @ResponseStatus
docs.text:
Scenario: You have legacy domain exceptions annotated with @ResponseStatus and want the library to handle them automatically without modifications.

Source: CustomConflictException.java

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CONFLICT)
public class CustomConflictException extends RuntimeException {
    public CustomConflictException(String message) {
        super(message);
    }
}

Usage in a controller:

@GetMapping("/annotated")
public void throwAnnotated() {
    throw new CustomConflictException("This resource is currently being edited.");
}

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:conflict",
  "title": "Conflict",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "This resource is currently being edited.",
  "code": "CONFLICT",
  "traceId": "..."
}

The library reads the @ResponseStatus annotation from your exception class and uses it to set the HTTP status and derive the type URN.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: This section covers common questions from different engineering roles regarding the architectural decisions and operational behavior of the api-standard-spring-boot-starter.

docs.title: Q: Can I exclude specific controllers from the global error handler?
docs.text: A: No. The GlobalExceptionHandler is annotated with @RestControllerAdvice without a basePackages restriction, meaning it applies globally to the entire Spring context. If you need custom error handling for a specific controller, you must define an @ExceptionHandler method directly inside that specific controller. Spring will give your local handler precedence over the global advice.

docs.title: Q: Why do we use RFC 9457 (ProblemDetail) instead of a custom JSON format?
docs.text: A: To avoid "contract drift". In large enterprise ecosystems, every team tends to invent their own error JSON structure ({"error":...}, {"status":...}, {"message":...}). By adopting an IETF standard (RFC 9457), API consumers (like Frontend apps or external gateways) can write a single, universal error parser that works across all microservices.

docs.title: Q: Does generating this JSON add latency to the API?
docs.text: A: The JSON serialization (ProblemDetailService) and the enrichment pipeline have negligible overhead ($O(1)$ complexity). The actual performance cost during an error comes from the JVM generating the stack trace when the exception is initially thrown. Therefore, you should never use BusinessException for normal application control flow.

docs.title: Q: How do I correlate these error responses with my logs in Datadog, ELK, or Grafana?
docs.text: A: The starter automatically runs the TraceIdEnricher. If a trace ID is present in the SLF4J Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC), it will be injected into the error JSON under the traceId key. To complete the correlation, ensure your logback-spring.xml or logging configuration includes the MDC variable (e.g., [%X{traceId}]) so your logs match the JSON returned to the client.

docs.title: Q: How does the library prevent leaking PII in validation errors?
docs.text: A: When a MethodArgumentNotValidException occurs, the starter exposes the field names that failed validation. To prevent leaking sensitive data (like a user submitting an invalid password), the library employs a DefaultRedactionPolicy. By default, it masks the values of fields named password, token, secret, creditCard, cvv, ssn, and authorization.

docs.title: Q: Can I change which fields are masked by the redaction policy?
docs.text:
A: Yes. You can override the default list in your application.yml:

api:
  standard:
    redaction:
      enabled: true
      mask: "***"
      fields:
        - "password"
        - "myCustomSecretToken"

docs.title: Installation & Setup
docs.text: This guide covers how to install the api-standard-spring-boot-starter and the initial configuration options available.

docs.title: Minimum Requirements
docs.text:
The library has been verified with the following stack:

Requirement Version Notes Java 21 Uses features like Pattern Matching and Records. Spring Boot 4.0.6 Verified with this specific version. Spring Web Included Designed for Spring MVC applications.

docs.title: Compatibility Matrix
docs.text: [!WARNING] Limited Verification: The current project codebase and documentation explicitly reference Spring Boot 4.0.6 and Java 21. Compatibility with older versions (such as Spring Boot 3.x or Java 17) or other frameworks has not been verified or documented in the repository.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Add the dependency to your build system. Since this is a Spring Boot starter, it will auto-configure itself once present on the classpath.

MavenGradle

Add the following to your pom.xml:

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.saul789</groupId>
    <artifactId>api-standard-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
    <version>2.0.0</version>
</dependency>

Add the following to your build.gradle:

implementation 'io.github.saul789:api-standard-spring-boot-starter:2.0.0'

docs.title: Initial Configuration
docs.text:
You can customize the behavior of the starter by adding the following properties to your application.yml or application.properties.

Here are all the properties available in the source code (ApiStandardProperties.java):

api:
  standard:
    errors:
      # Base URI for the 'type' field in ProblemDetail responses.
      type-base-uri: "urn:problem-type:"

      # Map of error codes to custom documentation URLs.
      type-overrides:
        # Example:
        # NOT_FOUND: "https://docs.example.com/errors/not-found"

    degraded-mode:
      # Whether to enable the degraded mode filter and enricher.
      enabled: true

      # CPU usage threshold percentage to trigger degraded mode.
      cpu-threshold: 80.0

      # Whether to show the 'degraded' flag in the JSON response.
      show-in-json: false

      # Whether to show the 'X-API-Degraded' header in the response.
      show-in-header: true

    redaction:
      # Whether to enable the PII redaction engine.
      enabled: true

      # The mask to replace sensitive field values with.
      mask: "[REDACTED]"

      # List of field names whose values should be redacted.
      fields:
        - "password"
        - "token"
        - "secret"
        - "creditCard"
        - "cvv"
        - "ssn"
        - "authorization"

docs.title: JS Ecosystem & Platform Compatibility (SSR/ESM/CJS)
docs.text:
[!NOTE] Not Applicable: This is a Java/Spring Boot server-side library. JavaScript module systems (ESM, CJS) and Server-Side Rendering (SSR) paradigms do not apply.

WebFlux Support: Support for Spring WebFlux is not explicitly implemented or tested in the current codebase (the current handlers are based on Spring MVC and HttpServletRequest).

docs.title: Issue: Circular Dependency
docs.text:
• Symptom: Spring fails to start with a circular reference error involving GlobalExceptionHandler or security filters.
  • Root Cause: Custom security configurations injecting the exception handler too early.
  • Solution: Ensure your security configuration does not eagerly depend on the error handling beans or adjust the @Order of your filters.

docs.title: Issue: CPU Load Not Available
docs.text:
• Symptom: Degraded mode is enabled but never triggers or logs warnings.
  • Root Cause: The underlying operating system or JVM does not support OperatingSystemMXBean.getCpuLoad() (returns -1).
  • Solution: In these environments, the library falls back to assuming normal load. Custom implementation of SystemLoadMonitor is required if you need to use another metric.

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: This guide helps you transition from vanilla Spring Boot's default error handling to the structured, RFC 9457-compliant api-standard-spring-boot-starter.

docs.title: 1. The Breaking Change: Response Payload
docs.text:
The most significant breaking change is the JSON structure returned to your clients.

Old (Vanilla Spring Boot) 

{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-18T10:00:00.000+00:00",
  "status": 400,
  "error": "Bad Request",
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "path": "/api/v1/resource"
}

New (API Standard Starter / RFC 9457) 

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:validation-error",
  "title": "Validation Error",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Validation failed",
  "instance": "/api/v1/resource",
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-18T10:00:00Z"
}

Frontend Impact: Any frontend application, mobile app, or API gateway that parses error messages must be updated to read the detail property instead of message, and title instead of error.

docs.title: Step 1: Remove Custom Global Handlers
docs.text: If your project currently has a custom @ControllerAdvice or @RestControllerAdvice that catches Exception.class or RuntimeException.class, you should remove it or restrict its scope. Otherwise, it will compete with the starter's GlobalExceptionHandler.

docs.title: Step 2: Adopt BusinessException
docs.text: Find your custom domain exceptions (e.g., UserNotFoundException, InvalidPaymentException). Refactor them to either extend BusinessException directly or map them to the canonical ErrorCode values provided by the library.

docs.title: Step 3: Update Integration Tests
docs.text: If you have integration tests (@SpringBootTest with MockMvc) that assert specific JSON paths (like $.message), you must update them: * Change $.message to $.detail. * Change $.error to $.title. * Change $.path to $.instance.

docs.title: 3. Gradual Rollout Strategy
docs.text:
If you have a large microservices architecture, do not attempt a "big bang" migration.

  1. Phase 1: Dual-Parser on Frontend. Update your Frontend HTTP interceptors (e.g., Axios, Fetch) to gracefully handle both formats. Check for the existence of type or detail to determine if the response is RFC 9457.
  2. Phase 2: Opt-in Services. Add the starter dependency to non-critical or newly created microservices first.
  3. Phase 3: Core Services. Migrate your core services and legacy monoliths.
  4. Phase 4: Cleanup. Remove the legacy parsers from the frontend.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide will help you create a minimal, realistic project to see the api-standard-spring-boot-starter in action.

docs.title: 1. Project Structure
docs.text:
A typical Spring Boot project using this starter looks like this:

my-api/
├── pom.xml (or build.gradle)
└── src/
    └── main/
        ├── java/
        │   └── com/example/demo/
        │       ├── DemoApplication.java
        │       └── controller/
        │           └── DemoController.java
        └── resources/
            └── application.yml

docs.title: 2. Implementation
docs.text:
We will use the native BusinessException and ErrorCode provided by the library to simulate a business rule violation (e.g., trying to create a resource that already exists).

Create the controller in DemoController.java:

package com.example.demo.controller;

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.BusinessException;
import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ErrorCode;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class DemoController {

    @GetMapping("/api/test-error")
    public void triggerError() {
        // Line-by-line explanation:
        // 1. We throw a BusinessException provided by the starter.
        // 2. We pass the canonical ErrorCode.CONFLICT (maps to 409).
        // 3. We provide a clear, user-friendly message.
        // 4. We set the HTTP status to CONFLICT (409).
        throw new BusinessException(
            ErrorCode.CONFLICT, 
            "The requested resource is already in use.",
            HttpStatus.CONFLICT
        );
    }
}

docs.title: 3. The Runtime Flow
docs.text:
When a client makes a request to /api/test-error, the following sequence occurs automatically without any extra code:

  1. Exception Thrown: DemoController throws BusinessException.
  2. Interception: The library's GlobalExceptionHandler (registered with the lowest precedence) catches the exception.
  3. Processing: ProblemDetailService starts building the RFC 9457 response.
  4. Enrichment Pipeline: The library executes the active enrichers present in the codebase:
    • StandardMetadataEnricher: Adds the machine-readable code and the timestamp.
    • TraceIdEnricher: Extracts the trace ID from the log MDC and injects it.
  5. Response: A ProblemDetail JSON is serialized and returned to the client.

docs.title: 4. Expected Result
docs.text:
Make a request to the endpoint (e.g., using curl). The starter will intercept the exception and return a clean, structured RFC 9457 compliant JSON:

{
  "type": "urn:problem-type:conflict",
  "title": "Conflict",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "The requested resource is already in use.",
  "instance": "/api/test-error",
  "code": "CONFLICT",
  "traceId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-18T21:34:00Z"
}

This ensures that all errors in your application follow the exact same contract.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This guide helps you diagnose and fix common issues you might encounter when integrating the api-standard-spring-boot-starter.

docs.title: Diagnostic Table
docs.text: Symptom Probable Root Cause Solution traceId is missing in the JSON The SLF4J MDC is empty when the error occurs. Ensure you have a tracing library installed (like Micrometer Tracing) or manually populate MDC.put("traceId", ...) in a prior filter. Also, verify the exception didn't happen in a background thread that lost the MDC context. Response is HTML instead of JSON The client is requesting HTML, or you used @Controller instead of @RestController. Ensure the client sends Accept: application/json. Verify your controllers are annotated with @RestController. Custom ProblemDetailEnricher doesn't execute Spring Boot did not detect your bean. Verify your enricher class is annotated with @Component and is located within a package covered by your @SpringBootApplication component scan. BusinessException returns HTTP 500 instead of 4xx The exception was caught and wrapped by a transaction boundary or proxy. Spring's @Transactional proxies might wrap checked exceptions in an UndeclaredThrowableException. Since BusinessException is a RuntimeException, ensure no intermediate aspect is swallowing and re-throwing it generically. Degraded mode (X-API-Degraded) never triggers The underlying OS or JVM does not expose CPU metrics. If OperatingSystemMXBean.getCpuLoad() returns -1, the library defaults to "normal load". You must implement a custom SystemLoadMonitor if you need to use a different metric (like memory or active threads). Validation errors don't show specific fields The exception thrown was not MethodArgumentNotValidException. Ensure you are using @Valid or @Validated on your controller payload parameters, rather than manually throwing generic exceptions.

docs.title: Debugging Deep-Dive
docs.text: If the table above doesn't resolve your issue, you can enable deep trace logging to see exactly how the library is evaluating the exceptions.

docs.title: Enabling Trace Logs
docs.text:
Add the following to your application.yml (development only):

logging:
  level:
    io.github.saul789.api.standard: TRACE

This will log: * Whenever the GlobalExceptionHandler intercepts an error. * The exact ErrorCode resolved. * Failures when trying to resolve custom URI types or request paths.

docs.title: Advanced Guides
docs.text: This section covers advanced enterprise scenarios. Following strict documentation guidelines, we only document integrations and patterns explicitly supported by the current codebase.

docs.title: 1. Observability and Tracing (MDC)
docs.text: The library natively integrates with SLF4J's Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC) via the TraceIdEnricher. If your application uses Spring Cloud Sleuth or Micrometer Tracing (OpenTelemetry/Zipkin), the traceId is automatically injected into the MDC. The starter reads this value and injects it into every error response, ensuring end-to-end correlation between logs, APM tools (like Datadog or New Relic), and client responses.

docs.title: 2. Microservices Integration (Feign)
docs.text: The starter includes a FeignExceptionHandler that activates automatically if feign.FeignException is on the classpath. * Behavior: When an upstream service fails (e.g., returns a 400 or 500), the handler intercepts the FeignException. * Bubbling: It parses the remote error body (expecting an RFC 9457 JSON). If the remote service returned a detail and code, this starter extracts them and bubbles them up to the caller, preventing context loss.

docs.title: 3. Resiliency (Circuit Breaker & Rate Limiting)
docs.text: The GlobalExceptionHandler natively detects and handles Resilience4j exceptions: * CallNotPermittedException (Circuit Breaker Open) -> Returns 503 Service Unavailable with SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE code. * RequestNotPermitted / BulkheadFullException (Rate Limiting) -> Returns 429 Too Many Requests with TOO_MANY_REQUESTS code.

docs.title: Unsupported Capabilities
docs.text:
The following topics are not currently supported natively by the starter and require custom implementation at the application level:

  • Serverless / Edge Runtime: The library relies on Servlet API (HttpServletRequest) and Spring MVC @ControllerAdvice, making it incompatible with pure edge runtimes or non-servlet Serverless environments.
  • Multitenancy: No native tenant-awareness. Can be achieved by writing a custom ProblemDetailEnricher.
  • Feature Flags: No native integration with LaunchDarkly, Unleash, etc.
  • Native OpenTelemetry Auto-Instrumentation: The library relies on MDC, not direct OTel spans.

docs.title: Customizing the Platform 🛠️
docs.text: While the starter provides powerful defaults (like Trace ID injection, Degraded Mode, and Redaction), you will inevitably need to add your own organization's custom logic to the API responses.

docs.title: The ProblemDetailEnricher SPI
docs.text:
The platform exposes an extremely simple Service Provider Interface (SPI): the ProblemDetailEnricher interface.

Because the starter relies on Spring's auto-wiring of lists (List<ProblemDetailEnricher>), all you need to do is register a new Spring Bean that implements this interface. The platform will automatically discover it and run it for every API error!

docs.title: Example: Injecting a Cloud Region ID
docs.text:
Imagine your organization requires every API error to expose which AWS region or Kubernetes cluster served the request.

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ProblemDetailEnricher;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import java.util.Locale;

@Component
public class CloudRegionEnricher implements ProblemDetailEnricher {

    @Override
    public void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale, Exception ex) {
        // Read from an environment variable or system property
        String region = System.getenv().getOrDefault("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1");

        // Inject the property into the ProblemDetail JSON
        problem.setProperty("cloudRegion", region);
    }

    @Override
    public int order() {
        // Defines the execution order relative to other enrichers.
        // Lower numbers run first.
        return 50; 
    }
}

docs.title: Order of Execution
docs.text: The starter uses the order() method to determine execution sequence. For reference, here are the default enrichers and their orders: - StandardMetadataEnricher (order = 0) - TraceIdEnricher (order = 10) - AnnotationEnricher (order = 20) - DegradedModeEnricher (order = 100) - RedactionEnricher (order = Integer.MAX_VALUE) - Always runs last to mask data added by previous enrichers.

docs.title: Bypassing the Platform
docs.text:
If you have a specific controller where you do not want the Global Exception Handler to interfere (for example, a legacy webhook that expects a raw XML string error), you can simply handle the exception manually within the controller using a local @ExceptionHandler or standard try/catch.

Spring MVC prioritizes local @ExceptionHandler methods inside a @RestController over the @RestControllerAdvice provided by this starter.

docs.title: Personalizando la Plataforma 🛠️
docs.text: Aunque el starter ofrece potentes valores predeterminados (como inyección de Trace ID, Modo Degradado y Redacción), inevitablemente necesitarás agregar la lógica personalizada de tu organización a las respuestas de la API.

docs.title: El SPI ProblemDetailEnricher
docs.text:
La plataforma expone una Service Provider Interface (SPI) extremadamente simple: la interfaz ProblemDetailEnricher.

Debido a que el starter depende del auto-cableado (autowiring) de listas de Spring (List<ProblemDetailEnricher>), todo lo que necesitas hacer es registrar un nuevo Spring Bean que implemente esta interfaz. ¡La plataforma lo descubrirá automáticamente y lo ejecutará para cada error de la API!

docs.title: Ejemplo: Inyectando el ID de Región Cloud
docs.text:
Imagina que tu organización requiere que cada error de la API exponga qué región de AWS o clúster de Kubernetes sirvió la petición.

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ProblemDetailEnricher;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import java.util.Locale;

@Component
public class CloudRegionEnricher implements ProblemDetailEnricher {

    @Override
    public void enrich(ProblemDetail problem, HttpServletRequest request, Locale locale, Exception ex) {
        // Leer de una variable de entorno o propiedad del sistema
        String region = System.getenv().getOrDefault("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1");

        // Inyectar la propiedad en el JSON de ProblemDetail
        problem.setProperty("cloudRegion", region);
    }

    @Override
    public int order() {
        // Define el orden de ejecución relativo a otros enriquecedores.
        // Los números más bajos se ejecutan primero.
        return 50; 
    }
}

docs.title: Orden de Ejecución
docs.text: El starter utiliza el método order() para determinar la secuencia de ejecución. Como referencia, estos son los enriquecedores por defecto y sus órdenes: - StandardMetadataEnricher (order = 0) - TraceIdEnricher (order = 10) - AnnotationEnricher (order = 20) - DegradedModeEnricher (order = 100) - RedactionEnricher (order = Integer.MAX_VALUE) - Siempre se ejecuta al final para enmascarar datos agregados por enriquecedores previos.

docs.title: Evadiendo la Plataforma
docs.text:
Si tienes un controlador específico donde no deseas que el Manejador Global de Excepciones interfiera (por ejemplo, un webhook heredado que espera un error en formato XML crudo), simplemente puedes manejar la excepción manualmente dentro del controlador usando un @ExceptionHandler local o el clásico try/catch.

Spring MVC prioriza los métodos @ExceptionHandler locales dentro de un @RestController sobre el @RestControllerAdvice proporcionado por este starter.

docs.title: Error Intelligence Platform 🧠
docs.text: The V2 release transforms this starter into a full Error Intelligence Platform. It protects your system under load and sanitizes data before it reaches the client.

docs.title: 🔒 Redaction Engine (Data Masking)
docs.text:
API error responses are a common source of accidental data leaks (PII/Credentials). The Redaction Engine intercepts every ProblemDetail and masks sensitive fields inside validation errors or exposed properties.

Note: This protects any downstream logs that serialize the error response, but it is not an SLF4J appender (it won't mask manual log.info("password:...") statements).

api:
  standard:
    redaction:
      enabled: true
      fields: "password, token, secret, credit_card, apiKey, cvv"
      mask: "***"

JSON Output Example (Validation Error): 

{
  "type": "https://api.domain.com/errors/validation",
  "title": "Validation Failed",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Invalid request body",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "password",
      "rejectedValue": "***",  // <--- Masked by Redaction Engine
      "message": "Password must contain at least 8 characters"
    }
  ],
  "traceId": "a1b2c3d4"
}

docs.title: 🎯 Opt-in Field Exposure
docs.text:
By default, the platform takes a "Secure by Default" approach: custom exception fields are NOT serialized into the JSON response to prevent accidental internal state leaks.

To expose a safe diagnostic field, annotate it with @ExposeToProblemDetail:

public class InsufficientFundsException extends BusinessException {

    // This will be added to the JSON as "balance": 10.50
    @ExposeToProblemDetail("balance") 
    private final BigDecimal currentBalance;

    // This will remain hidden
    private final String internalDatabaseId; 

    public InsufficientFundsException(BigDecimal balance, String dbId) {
        super("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "Not enough money", HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
        this.currentBalance = balance;
        this.internalDatabaseId = dbId;
    }
}

JSON Output Example: 

{
  "type": "https://api.domain.com/errors/insufficient-funds",
  "title": "Insufficient Funds",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "Not enough money",
  "balance": 10.50,         // <--- Exposed via @ExposeToProblemDetail
  "traceId": "f9e8d7c6"
  // Note: internalDatabaseId is safely omitted
}

docs.title: Exception Handling & i18n 🌐
docs.text: The core philosophy of this starter is that you should never manually build an error response. Just throw standard exceptions, and the platform will handle the HTTP mapping, RFC 9457 Problem Details generation, and multi-language translation.

docs.title: Built-in Exceptions
docs.text: The api-standard-core module provides base exceptions that you can use or extend:

docs.title: BusinessException
docs.text:
Used for expected business rule violations. Maps to 4xx status codes. 

// Using predefined Enum
throw new BusinessException(ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, "User ID 123 does not exist", HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND);

// Using a custom String code for business domain specific errors
throw new BusinessException("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "Not enough balance", HttpStatus.CONFLICT);

docs.title: ProblemException
docs.text:
Used for unexpected system failures. Maps to 5xx status codes. 

throw new ProblemException(ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR, "Failed to connect to database");

docs.title: Spring @Valid Support (Validation Errors)
docs.text: The GlobalExceptionHandler automatically intercepts MethodArgumentNotValidException. If you use @Valid on your request bodies, you don't need to do anything. The starter will return a 400 Bad Request with ErrorCode.VALIDATION_ERROR and a detailed array of the fields that failed.

docs.title: Customizing the type URI
docs.text:
By default, the type URL is generated using the base URI (from application.yml) + the kebab-case error code (e.g., urn:api:error:insufficient-funds).

You can override this on a per-exception basis using the @ProblemType annotation or the ProblemTypeProvider interface.

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ProblemType;
import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.BusinessException;

@ProblemType("https://developer.mycompany.com/errors/billing/funds")
public class InsufficientFundsException extends BusinessException {
    public InsufficientFundsException() {
        super("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "Not enough balance", HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
    }
}

docs.title: Automatic i18n (Translations)
docs.text:
You don't need to hardcode error messages. The GlobalExceptionHandler automatically intercepts exceptions and attempts to translate the detail and title using Spring's standard MessageSource.

  1. Throw an exception with an Error Code: 

    throw new BusinessException("USER_LOCKED", "User is locked out");

  2. Add a messages_es.properties in your resources: 

    error.USER_LOCKED.title=Usuario Bloqueado
error.USER_LOCKED.detail=El usuario ha excedido los intentos permitidos.

If a client sends the header Accept-Language: es-ES, the ProblemDetail JSON will automatically return the translated title and detail.

JSON Output Example (Accept-Language: es-ES): 

{
  "type": "urn:api:error:user-locked",
  "title": "Usuario Bloqueado",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "El usuario ha excedido los intentos permitidos.",
  "instance": "/api/auth/login",
  "code": "USER_LOCKED",
  "traceId": "9b8a7c6d"
}

docs.title: Exception Handling & i18n 🌐
docs.text: The core philosophy of this starter is that you should never manually build an error response. Just throw standard exceptions, and the platform will handle the HTTP mapping, RFC 9457 Problem Details generation, and multi-language translation.

docs.title: Built-in Exceptions
docs.text: The api-standard-core module provides base exceptions that you can use or extend:

docs.title: BusinessException
docs.text:
Used for expected business rule violations. Maps to 4xx status codes. 

// Using predefined Enum
throw new BusinessException(ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, "User ID 123 does not exist", HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND);

// Using a custom String code for business domain specific errors
throw new BusinessException("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "Not enough balance", HttpStatus.CONFLICT);

docs.title: ProblemException
docs.text:
Used for unexpected system failures. Maps to 5xx status codes. 

throw new ProblemException(ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR, "Failed to connect to database");

docs.title: Spring @Valid Support (Validation Errors)
docs.text: The GlobalExceptionHandler automatically intercepts MethodArgumentNotValidException. If you use @Valid on your request bodies, you don't need to do anything. The starter will return a 400 Bad Request with ErrorCode.VALIDATION_ERROR and a detailed array of the fields that failed.

docs.title: Customizing the type URI
docs.text:
By default, the type URL is generated using the base URI (from application.yml) + the kebab-case error code (e.g., urn:api:error:insufficient-funds).

You can override this on a per-exception basis using the @ProblemType annotation or the ProblemTypeProvider interface.

import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.ProblemType;
import io.github.saul789.api.standard.exception.BusinessException;

@ProblemType("https://developer.mycompany.com/errors/billing/funds")
public class InsufficientFundsException extends BusinessException {
    public InsufficientFundsException() {
        super("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "Not enough balance", HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
    }
}

docs.title: Observability & Tracing 🔭
docs.text: The starter comes batteries-included for Day 2 operations, giving your operations and SRE teams immediate visibility into your API's health.

docs.title: 📊 Micrometer Metrics Auto-Counters
docs.text:
If micrometer-core is on your classpath, the starter registers a MetricsEnricher. Every time a standardized error occurs, it increments a Micrometer counter named api.errors.total.

You can view these in Prometheus or Datadog, grouped by tags: - code: The Business ErrorCode (e.g., VALIDATION_ERROR, NOT_FOUND). - status: HTTP Status Code (e.g., 400). - method: HTTP Method (e.g., POST). - uri: Mapped Spring MVC Pattern (e.g., /users/{id}). Note: Raw URIs are converted to mapped patterns to prevent cardinality explosion in Prometheus.

docs.title: 🔍 Trace Context Propagation
docs.text:
Every incoming HTTP request is intercepted by the TraceContextFilter. 1. It looks for X-Trace-Id or b3 tracing headers. 2. If absent, it generates a new UUID. 3. It immediately injects this traceId into the SLF4J MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context). 4. The traceId is included in every RFC 9457 JSON error response.

This ensures that your logs and your client errors are perfectly correlated.

JSON Output Example: 

{
  "title": "Internal Server Error",
  "status": 500,
  "detail": "Database connection timeout",
  "traceId": "5f9b3b8c-1234-4a56-b789-abcdef123456" // <--- MDC traceId
}
